items.title: After the Burn
items.desc: Arrel feels the sealed cavity left by his first visible burn.
items.anchor_text: His skull throbbed. Not the clean pain of a headache but a deeper pressure, as if someone had scooped out a piece of his brain and left the cavity unsealed.

items.title: Ash That Remembers
items.desc: Warm ash dissolves against Arrel's skin.
items.anchor_text: A gray flake, lighter than dust, dissolving against his skin with a faint warmth that was not his own.

items.title: The Reach Before Memory
items.desc: Arrel's body recognizes Elia before his mind does.
items.anchor_text: His right hand twitched. It moved toward her before he could stop it, fingers uncurling from the sword grip, reaching for something his muscles remembered but his mind did not.

items.title: Initials in the Stump
items.desc: Two surviving initials hint at a forgotten bond.
items.anchor_text: Someone had carved letters into it once. The rain had eaten most of them, but two remained: A. E.

items.title: Amber Memory Shrine
items.desc: A forest shrine preserves memory as liquid amber.
items.anchor_text: Stones stacked in careful pyramids. Strips of cloth tied to branches. And in the center, a glass bottle filled with something that caught the dim light like liquid amber.

items.title: Bottled Memory Market
items.desc: Verdan sells impossible fragments of ordinary lives.
items.anchor_text: Stalls selling things that shouldn't exist, bottled laughter, crystallized grief, a child's first word trapped in resin and going for forty Grains.

items.title: Waiting Alcoves
items.desc: Buyers and sellers wait in the Sump's forgettable tunnels.
items.anchor_text: Alcoves lined the tunnel walls. In each one, someone waited. Buyers. Sellers. People whose faces you forgot the moment you looked away.

items.title: Malet from the Gray
items.desc: Malet appears as though the walls have produced him.
items.anchor_text: Malet appeared as if he had always been there. Small, thin, dressed in gray that matched the walls.

items.title: The Empty First Sword
items.desc: The first sword memory leaves only the shape of significance.
items.anchor_text: Then it left. Silent as a drawer closing. And where it had been, nothing. A space shaped like significance, emptied of content.

items.title: The Nameless Burner
items.desc: A burned-out survivor shows the human cost of the market.
items.anchor_text: His face was placid. Smooth. Not peaceful, empty. Like a mask worn by someone who had forgotten what expressions were for.

items.title: Waystation Through the Haze
items.desc: A forgotten station emerges from the Belt's haze.
items.anchor_text: Finally, a crumbling waystation appeared through the haze. A water tower listed sideways, its tank long dry.

items.title: Tobias Keeps Account
items.desc: Tobias measures residue where certainty has failed.
items.anchor_text: ...seven-point-three Grains per unit, adjusted for residue decay... no, that can't be right...

items.title: Warm Blank Book
items.desc: A blank book radiates the warmth of missing words.
items.anchor_text: Ah. You can see it too? Most people walk right past. That's a Blank Book.

items.title: Class Seven on the Wall
items.desc: A precise Bureau note turns Arrel into a classified subject.
items.anchor_text: The handwriting was precise, almost mechanical: 'Subject demonstrates Class Seven combustion efficiency.'

items.title: Three on the Belt
items.desc: Arrel, Elia, and Tobias leave the lonely station behind.
items.anchor_text: Arrel looked back at the waystation one last time. It sat alone on the Belt like a forgotten thought.

items.title: Memory Rain Shelter
items.desc: Ash-colored rain marks the party inside the Drift.
items.anchor_text: Rain began to fall. Not water. Ash-colored drops that left gray streaks on skin.

items.title: The Words Move
items.desc: Reading itself begins to slide out of Arrel's grasp.
items.anchor_text: The words are moving.

items.title: Anchor Tea and Thread
items.desc: Elia anchors Arrel through a small deliberate ritual.
items.anchor_text: Just sit.

items.title: Burner Classification
items.desc: Tobias explains the Bureau's seven classes of Burners.
items.anchor_text: The Bureau ranks Burners from Class One to Class Seven. Most never exceed Class Three.

items.title: A Table for Three
items.desc: A home memory survives as a table always set for three.
items.anchor_text: ...the table was always set for three.

items.title: City in the Bedrock
items.desc: The coast reveals where a city was pressed into stone.
items.anchor_text: Where the land forgot how to hold itself together. Cliffs sheared clean as if something had bitten through the bedrock.

items.title: Observer on the Ridge
items.desc: Kairos watches the party from a distant ridge.
items.anchor_text: A figure. Still as stone. Watching.

items.title: Warm Stone Echo
items.desc: Memory residue makes the ruined coast feel alive underhand.
items.anchor_text: Memory residue. This coastline was a city once. Thousands of people's lives, pressed into the bedrock. When the Void came, the stone absorbed what the people lost.

items.title: Parting Paths
items.desc: Elia weighs separation at the edge of the coast.
items.anchor_text: Elia stopped. Her eyes traced the cliff edge, then snapped back to the ridge behind them.

items.title: The First Impossible Color
items.desc: The Seam returns colors thought lost since the Collapse.
items.anchor_text: Between the gray cliffs, in a canyon that shouldn't have existed, light fell in shades that hadn't been seen since the Collapse.

items.title: Living Streets of the Seam
items.desc: A refuge proves that ordinary life can still be made real.
items.anchor_text: Buildings made of salvaged stone and driftwood, painted in colors that shouldn't still exist. Amber. Teal. A red so vivid it felt borrowed from a dream.

items.title: Sable's Seven-Lantern Briefing
items.desc: Sable marks the growing wound called BL-07.
items.anchor_text: Same thing. Listen, there's a Void Hole forming south of here. Designation BL-07.

items.title: The Impossible Garden
items.desc: A gold-veined flower remembers vanished sunlight.
items.anchor_text: White petals, veined with gold. It was warm to the touch, as if remembering sunlight from somewhere that no longer existed.

items.title: Stars Forgetting
items.desc: The sky loses stars while Elia asks Arrel to return.
items.anchor_text: The stars were going out. One by one. Like the sky was forgetting them.

items.title: At the Edge of BL-07
items.desc: Sable leads the party toward a wound in reality.
items.anchor_text: Ahead, a tear in the world. Not large, but growing. The edges flickered between here and nowhere.

items.title: The Last Survey Ridge
items.desc: The Bureau's maps stop at the threshold of the unknown.
items.anchor_text: The Bureau maps end exactly at this ridgeline. Beyond is classified, Level 9 clearance only.

items.title: The Cleaner's Confession
items.desc: Sable lays down the insignia of her former life.
items.anchor_text: Subsection Eleven. Memory Disposal. They called us Cleaners. We made people forget things the Authority didn't want remembered.

items.title: Controlled Burn Trial
items.desc: Sable tests whether Arrel can remain himself after burning.
items.anchor_text: Burn something. Right now. Deliberately. And hold yourself together after.

items.title: Twelve Names
items.desc: A cairn and its lanterns remember twelve erased lives.
items.anchor_text: A memorial cairn. Bureau standard. These names... they're the first expedition team. Twelve people. All erased.

items.title: Voices in the Echo Shell
items.desc: Ordinary fragments of erased people circle an opened shell.
items.anchor_text: There are people in here. Fragments of people. Dozens of them.

items.title: Entering the Memory Forest
items.desc: Concentric black trees close around the expedition.
items.anchor_text: This is the Memory Forest. The trees are what's left of the first settlement near BL-07.

items.title: The Child Without a Name
items.desc: A child's voice loops around a missing name.
items.anchor_text: Arrel held it to his ear. A child's voice, clearer than the others: 'I had a dog. His name was,  his name was...'

items.title: Eighteen Accelerating Rings
items.desc: Tobias measures how quickly the intervals are shrinking.
items.anchor_text: The intervals are decreasing. Ring one to ring two: eight years. Ring sixteen to seventeen: four months. It's accelerating.

items.title: The Searching Mother
items.desc: Muscle memory cradles a child who is no longer there.
items.anchor_text: She's looking for someone. A child. You can see it in the way her arms are held, muscle memory outlasting everything else.

items.title: Parasitic Heart
items.desc: The forest's root-heart feeds on memory residue.
items.anchor_text: We've reached it. The parasitic core. Every tree in this forest is connected to this point, a single organism feeding on memory residue.

items.title: The Equalized Waste
items.desc: Color and distance fail while a tether keeps two people together.
items.anchor_text: Welcome to the Waste. Everything here has been equalized.

items.title: The Living Compass
items.desc: A thread from Arrel's heart points toward BL-07.
items.anchor_text: I can feel where it is. BL-07. It's... that way.

items.title: Kairos's Convergence Model
items.desc: Kairos turns every erased route toward a single center.
items.anchor_text: Kairos. Taller than his silhouette on the coastal ridge. Dark coat, Bureau insignia, but modified. Gold thread where standard silver should be.

items.title: Eighteen Depth Markers
items.desc: Compressed rings become gravestones for erased generations.
items.anchor_text: These are depth markers. The closer to BL-07, the more compressed the residue. It's like tree rings but for destruction.

items.title: The First Void Witness
items.desc: A recovered thought remembers the first Void Hole opening.
items.anchor_text: He knelt and pressed his palm to the ground. A fragment surfaced: the last thought of someone who had stood here centuries ago, watching the first Void Hole open.

items.title: Path Made of Remembered Stone
items.desc: Arrel and Elia descend on stone remembered by the Void.
items.anchor_text: Each step took them deeper. Not into the ground. Into the absence of ground. The fragments they walked on were memories of stone, held together by the Void's habit of destruction.

items.title: Borrowed Grief
items.desc: Thousands of ordinary losses pass through Arrel at once.
items.anchor_text: Not words. Feelings. Borrowed grief that pressed against his ribs like an unwelcome hand.

items.title: Orphaned Lives
items.desc: The Void keeps memories whose owners no longer know them.
items.anchor_text: These are the memories the Void has consumed. It doesn't destroy them, it KEEPS them. Like a collection.

items.title: Before the Core
items.desc: Elia asks Arrel to enter the final choice as himself.
items.anchor_text: Arrel. Before we go further. There's something I need to say.

items.title: Name or Weave
items.desc: The final choice contrasts solitary burning with shared remembrance.
items.anchor_text: Wait. You're still... you. After all of it, you kept the things that matter. The name. The sword. My hands on yours. Maybe you don't have to choose what to lose. Maybe you offer what you kept.
